- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for high sentiment periods.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 78), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment drops.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid mean reversion underestimation.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day horizon in early cycles; apply 1–2% downward bias for 30d forecasts if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or 0.33 values (neutral/negative), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to catch mean reversion.
- When sentiment spikes to 1.00 and price is rising, model often overreacts; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
